descriptionChirho: A young shoot or branch growing from a plant or tree, used literally of botanical growth. All occurrences carry pronominal suffixes ('his shoots,' 'its shoots') referring to the parent plant. Multilingual evidence converges: Arabic فُرُوع (furū', 'branches'), Spanish retoño/renuevos ('sprouts/new shoots'), Hindi शाखाएँ/डालियां (shākhāẽ/ḍāliyā̃, 'branches'), Korean 어린 싹/가지 (eorin ssak/gaji, 'young shoot/branch'), Swahili machipukizi ('sprouts'). The conjunction-prefixed form (S101560) is merely a syntactic variant with waw-copulative, not a distinct meaning.
